name: Helm checks
description: Lint, render, validate and package the HugeGraph Helm chart
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
  # azure/setup-helm is not on the ASF-approved actions allowlist, which
  # fails the workflow at startup; install the pinned release directly.
  - name: install helm
    shell: 'bash -e {0}'
    run: |
      curl -fsSLo /tmp/helm.tgz https://get.helm.sh/helm-v3.16.2-linux-amd64.tar.gz
      echo "9318379b847e333460d33d291d4c088156299a26cd93d570a7f5d0c36e50b5bb  /tmp/helm.tgz" | sha256sum -c -
      tar -xzf /tmp/helm.tgz -C /tmp
      sudo install -m 0755 /tmp/linux-amd64/helm /usr/local/bin/helm
      helm version

  - name: helm lint
    shell: 'bash -e {0}'
    run: |
      helm lint helm/hugegraph
      helm lint helm/hugegraph -f helm/hugegraph/values-single.yaml
      helm lint helm/hugegraph -f helm/hugegraph/values-cluster.yaml
      helm lint helm/hugegraph -f helm/hugegraph/values-strict.yaml

  - name: packaged chart regression
    shell: 'bash -e {0}'
    run: python3 -m unittest discover -s helm -p 'test_helm_package.py' -v

  - name: helm unittest
    shell: 'bash -e {0}'
    run: |
      # v1.0.0 is the newest helm-unittest whose plugin.yaml Helm 3.16.2 can
      # parse (v1.1.x adds a platformHooks field that 3.16.2 rejects).
      # Pinned by the tag's commit so a moved tag cannot change what runs.
      helm plugin install https://github.com/helm-unittest/helm-unittest.git \
        --version ddd5feaa9465e7a3591792524ce7f441d4c5157e
      helm unittest helm/hugegraph

  - name: helm template
    shell: 'bash -e {0}'
    run: |
      for preset in "" "-f helm/hugegraph/values-single.yaml" "-f helm/hugegraph/values-cluster.yaml" "-f helm/hugegraph/values-strict.yaml"; do
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # $preset intentionally splits into flags
        helm template ci helm/hugegraph $preset > /dev/null
      done
      # Positive coverage for every hubble wrapper branch: pd mode with
      # auth, direct mode with a custom port, and a TLS-less ingress with
      # ordinary HTTP configuration, without acknowledgement flags.
      helm template ci helm/hugegraph \
        --set hubble.enabled=true \
        --set server.auth.enabled=true \
        --set server.auth.admin.existingSecret=ci-auth > /dev/null
      helm template ci helm/hugegraph \
        --set hubble.enabled=true \
        --set hubble.allowWithoutServerAuth=true \
        --set hubble.mode=direct \
        --set hubble.port=9090 \
        --set hubble.persistence.enabled=true \
        --set hubble.ingress.enabled=true \
        --set hubble.ingress.allowPlainHttp=true > /dev/null
      # PD sharding knobs rendered as -D system properties, including
      # the values-file shape where the count arrives as a numeric string
      helm template ci helm/hugegraph \
        --set pd.partition.defaultShardCount=3 \
        --set pd.partition.storeMaxShardCount=12 > /dev/null
      helm template ci helm/hugegraph \
        --set-string pd.partition.defaultShardCount=3 > /dev/null
      # The derived shard count and the raft whitelist and RPC-timeout flags must land in
      # the PD JAVA_OPTS verbatim: shard count 3 on the default topology,
      # 1 on the single-node preset, whitelist disabled in both.
      helm template ci helm/hugegraph \
        | grep -qF 'value: "-Dpartition.default-shard-count=3 -Draft.ip-whitelist.enabled=false -Draft.rpc-timeout=3000"'
      helm template ci helm/hugegraph -f helm/hugegraph/values-single.yaml \
        | grep -qF 'value: "-Dpartition.default-shard-count=1 -Draft.ip-whitelist.enabled=false -Draft.rpc-timeout=3000"'
      # The stock distributed install must put every Server replica on
      # the shared PD graph catalog, even without Hubble. Auth is on by
      # default, so the chart-managed admin Secret must render too.
      DEFAULT=$(helm template ci helm/hugegraph)
      grep -qF "printf 'usePD=true\\n'" <<<"$DEFAULT"
      grep -qF "printf 'pd.peers=%s\\n' \"\${HG_SERVER_PD_PEERS}\"" \
        <<<"$DEFAULT"
      grep -qF 'value: "ci-hugegraph-pd-0.ci-hugegraph-pd.default.svc:8686,ci-hugegraph-pd-1.ci-hugegraph-pd.default.svc:8686,ci-hugegraph-pd-2.ci-hugegraph-pd.default.svc:8686"' \
        <<<"$DEFAULT"
      grep -qE '^kind: Secret$' <<<"$DEFAULT"
      grep -qF 'name: ci-admin' <<<"$DEFAULT"
      grep -qF 'name: ci-auth-token' <<<"$DEFAULT"
      # A YAML-coercible Secret key must render quoted, or the API
      # server stores the key as a boolean and the pods cannot find it.
      helm template ci helm/hugegraph --set-string server.auth.admin.key=on \
        | grep -qF '"on":'
      # The install render must hash the generated credentials it writes:
      # the rollout checksums equal sha256(name|key|sha256(value)) over
      # the rendered Secret data, so the first upgrade, which reads the
      # same values back through lookup, renders the same checksums and
      # rolls nothing.
      python3 - <<'PY'
      import hashlib, base64, subprocess, yaml
      out = subprocess.check_output(['helm', 'template', 'ci', 'helm/hugegraph'])
      docs = [d for d in yaml.safe_load_all(out) if d]
      h = lambda s: hashlib.sha256(s.encode()).hexdigest()
      sec = {d['metadata']['name']: d['data'] for d in docs if d['kind'] == 'Secret'}
      val = lambda n, k: base64.b64decode(sec[n][k]).decode()
      pd = next(d for d in docs if d['kind'] == 'StatefulSet' and d['metadata']['name'] == 'ci-hugegraph-pd')
      srv = next(d for d in docs if d['kind'] == 'Deployment' and d['metadata']['name'] == 'ci-hugegraph-server')
      ann = lambda d, k: d['spec']['template']['metadata']['annotations'][k]
      assert ann(pd, 'checksum/pd-auth') == h('ci-pd-auth|secret-key|' + h(val('ci-pd-auth', 'secret-key')))
      assert ann(srv, 'checksum/pd-auth') == ann(pd, 'checksum/pd-auth')
      assert ann(srv, 'checksum/auth') == h('ci-admin|password|ci-auth-token|token_secret|'
                                           + h(val('ci-admin', 'password')) + '|' + h(val('ci-auth-token', 'token_secret')))
      print('install-time checksums match the generated Secret values')
      services = {d['metadata']['name']: d['spec'] for d in docs if d['kind'] == 'Service'}
      assert services['ci-hugegraph-server']['type'] == 'NodePort'
      assert services['ci-hugegraph-hubble']['type'] == 'NodePort'
      assert services['ci-hugegraph-pd-client']['type'] == 'ClusterIP'
      for name in ('ci-hugegraph-server', 'ci-hugegraph-hubble'):
          assert 'nodePort' not in services[name]['ports'][0]
      sts = [d for d in docs if d['kind'] == 'StatefulSet']
      assert sum(int(d['spec']['replicas']) * len(d['spec'].get('volumeClaimTemplates', []))
                 for d in sts) + sum(d['kind'] == 'PersistentVolumeClaim' for d in docs) == 7
      assert not any(d['kind'] == 'NetworkPolicy' for d in docs)
      assert not any('curlimages/' in str(d) for d in docs)
      print('easy defaults: three-member groups, seven volumes and direct HTTP NodePorts')
      PY

  - name: reject invalid values
    shell: 'bash -e {0}'
    run: |
      # Each case must fail to render; the schema and helpers are the
      # contract. `! cmd` alone is NOT enforced under `set -e` (errexit
      # ignores inverted commands), so every case checks explicitly.
      must_fail() {
        if helm template ci helm/hugegraph "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          echo "expected render failure for: $*" >&2
          exit 1
        fi
      }
      # Kubernetes permits successThreshold > 1 only for readiness.
      for component in pd store server hubble; do
        for probe in startup liveness; do
          must_fail --set "${component}.probes.${probe}.successThreshold=2"
        done
        helm template ci helm/hugegraph \
          --set "${component}.probes.readiness.successThreshold=2" > /dev/null
      done
      # These deployment inputs must serialize unchanged through the properties reader.
      must_fail --set-string server.serviceId=café
      must_fail --set-string server.serviceId=😀
      must_fail --set-string "$(printf 'server.serviceId=ops\tteam')"
      # Match the Server API graph-space names, including its 48-character limit.
      must_fail --set-string server.graphSpace=TeamA
      must_fail --set-string server.graphSpace=team-a
      must_fail --set-string server.graphSpace=1team
      graph_space_max=$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..48})
      helm template ci helm/hugegraph --set-string "server.graphSpace=${graph_space_max}" > /dev/null
      must_fail --set-string "server.graphSpace=${graph_space_max}a"
      # The hook queries an explicit, fully qualified existing graph binding.
      must_fail --set-string server.testGraphAlias=
      must_fail --set-string server.testGraphAlias=team_a
      must_fail --set-string server.testGraphAlias=team_a-demo-name
      must_fail --set-string "server.testGraphAlias=team_a-demo'"
      graph_name_max=$(printf 'g%.0s' {1..48})
      helm template ci helm/hugegraph \
        --set-string "server.testGraphAlias=${graph_space_max}-${graph_name_max}" > /dev/null
      must_fail --set-string "server.testGraphAlias=${graph_space_max}a-demo"
      must_fail --set-string "server.testGraphAlias=team_a-${graph_name_max}g"
      must_fail --set pd.replicas=100
      must_fail --set pd.pdb.minAvailable=3
      must_fail --set server.hpa.enabled=true
      must_fail \
        --set server.hpa.enabled=true \
        --set server.hpa.minReplicas=2 \
        --set server.resources.requests.cpu=100m \
        --set server.pdb.enabled=true \
        --set server.pdb.minAvailable=2
      must_fail --set server.auth.enabled=true --set server.auth.admin.autoGenerate=false --set server.auth.token.autoGenerate=false
      # pd.auth with every source disabled fails the schema anyOf; the
      # unit framework at v1.0.0 cannot match schema aborts, so the case
      # lives here.
      must_fail --set pd.auth.autoGenerate=false
      # Commons Configuration trims a properties value, so a credential
      # with surrounding whitespace would be stored in the Secret and
      # applied to the account without it. The schema rejects both ends;
      # these are schema aborts, so they live here rather than in the
      # unit suite. --set-string keeps the value a string.
      must_fail --set-string "server.auth.admin.password=[REDACTED] "
      must_fail --set-string "$(printf 'server.auth.admin.password=[REDACTED]')"
      must_fail --set-string "pd.auth.value=review-secret "
      # An inner space in the admin password fails too: the image
      # entrypoint stores it with a backslash before each space, so the
      # account would answer 401 to the configured value. The PD secret
      # is not written by that encoder, so its inner space stays legal.
      must_fail --set-string "server.auth.admin.password=review secret"
      helm template ci helm/hugegraph \
        --set-string "pd.auth.value=review secret" >/dev/null
      # The Server decodes Basic-auth credentials as ASCII, so a non-ASCII
      # admin password would be applied and then answer 401 to every
      # request; the schema refuses it before install, as it already
      # does for the PD REST secret. Backslashes and tabs go the same way.
      must_fail --set-string "server.auth.admin.password=密码abc"
      must_fail --set-string "server.auth.admin.password=café"
      # --set unescapes a single backslash, so the literal needs two.
      must_fail --set-string 'server.auth.admin.password=[REDACTED]'
      must_fail --set-string "$(printf 'server.auth.admin.password=[REDACTED]')"
      must_fail --set-string "pd.auth.value=密码abc"
      # The Server splits the decoded credential on every colon (400).
      must_fail --set-string 'server.auth.admin.password=[REDACTED]'
      helm template ci helm/hugegraph \
        --set-string "server.auth.admin.password=[REDACTED]" >/dev/null
      # Auth defaults to on, so Hubble alone is valid; refuse Hubble only
      # when authentication is explicitly disabled.
      must_fail --set hubble.enabled=true --set server.auth.enabled=false
      A=(--set hubble.enabled=true --set hubble.allowWithoutServerAuth=true)
      must_fail "${A[@]}" --set hubble.port=0
      must_fail "${A[@]}" \
        --set hubble.persistence.enabled=true \
        --set hubble.persistence.size=""
      must_fail "${A[@]}" --set hubble.service.type=ClusterIP --set hubble.service.nodePort=30080
      # HTTP is supported directly in both modes. Component choices take
      # precedence over mode defaults and require no acknowledgement.
      for mode in easy strict; do
        for component in pd server hubble; do
          for kind in NodePort LoadBalancer; do
            helm template ci helm/hugegraph --set "mode=$mode" \
              --set "${component}.service.type=$kind" > /dev/null
          done
        done
        helm template ci helm/hugegraph --set "mode=$mode" \
          --set server.ingress.enabled=true \
          --set hubble.ingress.enabled=true > /dev/null
      done
      must_fail "${A[@]}" --set hubble.mode=bogus
      must_fail "${A[@]}" --set hubble.image.tag=""
      # When UI is explicitly disabled, stale credentials may remain unused.
      helm template ci helm/hugegraph --set hubble.enabled=false \
        --set server.auth.enabled=false \
        --set server.auth.admin.password=[REDACTED] \
        --set server.auth.token.value=unused-token-that-is-at-least-32-bytes > /dev/null
      # Respect custom API-server NodePort ranges rather than assuming 30000+.
      helm template ci helm/hugegraph \
        --set server.service.nodePort=8802 \
        --set hubble.service.nodePort=8808 > /dev/null
      must_fail --set server.service.nodePort=65536
      must_fail --set server.probes.startup.failureThreshold=1
      # Kubernetes refuses a StatefulSet that carries rollingUpdate
      # options with updateStrategy OnDelete; the schema rejects the
      # combination up front (a schema abort, so it lives here).
      for component in pd store; do
        must_fail \
          --set "${component}.updateStrategy.type=OnDelete" \
          --set "${component}.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.partition=1"
        helm template ci helm/hugegraph \
          --set "${component}.updateStrategy.type=OnDelete" > /dev/null
      done
      # maxUnavailable above 1 lets the controller disrupt two members
      # of a three-member raft group or shard at once, and PDBs do not
      # constrain controller rollouts; the schema accepts integer 1 only.
      for component in pd store; do
        must_fail --set "${component}.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable=2"
        must_fail --set "${component}.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable=0"
        must_fail --set "${component}.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable=-1"
        must_fail --set-string "${component}.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable=67%"
        must_fail --set-string "${component}.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable=foo"
        must_fail --set-string "${component}.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable=1"
        helm template ci helm/hugegraph \
          --set "${component}.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable=1" > /dev/null
      done
      # PD PDB must keep the Raft majority: floor(replicas/2)+1
      must_fail --set pd.replicas=5 --set pd.pdb.minAvailable=2
      must_fail --set pd.replicas=4 --set pd.pdb.minAvailable=2
      helm template ci helm/hugegraph \
        --set pd.replicas=5 --set pd.pdb.minAvailable=3 > /dev/null
      helm template ci helm/hugegraph \
        --set pd.replicas=5 --set pd.pdb.minAvailable=4 > /dev/null
      # PD sharding knobs: empty or a positive integer; an explicit
      # shard count must be odd and stay within the store count
      must_fail --set pd.partition.defaultShardCount=0
      must_fail --set pd.partition.defaultShardCount=-1
      must_fail --set-string pd.partition.defaultShardCount=abc
      must_fail --set pd.partition.defaultShardCount=2
      must_fail --set pd.partition.defaultShardCount=5
      must_fail --set pd.partition.storeMaxShardCount=0
      # extraEnv must not override chart-managed variables
      must_fail --set 'server.extraEnv[0].name=HG_SERVER_INIT_STORE_ENABLED' \
        --set 'server.extraEnv[0].value=true'
      must_fail --set 'pd.extraEnv[0].name=HG_PD_RAFT_PEERS_LIST' \

  - name: helm test hook behaviour
    shell: bash
    run: |
      # The hook must fail when any one Server Pod cannot answer a
      # graph-bound Gremlin query, even while /versions and /graphs
      # answer 200 through the Service: a Server that started during a
      # PD roll stays in exactly that state for its whole life. Run the
      # rendered hook script against loopback fixtures.
      set -euo pipefail
      sudo sh -c 'echo "127.0.0.1 ci-hugegraph-server ci-hugegraph-server-headless" >> /etc/hosts'
      helm template ci helm/hugegraph -s templates/tests/test-connection.yaml > /tmp/hook.yaml
      python3 - <<'PY'
      import yaml
      d = yaml.safe_load(open('/tmp/hook.yaml'))
      open('/tmp/hook.sh', 'w').write(d['spec']['containers'][0]['command'][2])
      PY
      grep -q 'DEFAULT-hugegraph' /tmp/hook.sh
      # getent stub: the headless lookup answers with the fixture IPs.
      mkdir -p /tmp/stub
      printf '#!/bin/sh\nfor ip in ${STUB_IPS}; do printf "%%s STREAM host\\n" "$ip"; done\n' > /tmp/stub/getent
      chmod +x /tmp/stub/getent
      cat > /tmp/fixture.py <<'PY'
      import http.server, json, os, sys, threading, time
      calls = {}
      class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
          def _send(self, code, body):
              self.send_response(code)
              self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
              self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(body)))
              self.end_headers()
              self.wfile.write(body)
          def do_GET(self):
              self._send(200, b'{"versions":{}}')
          def do_POST(self):
              body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get('Content-Length', 0))))
              expected_alias = ('team_a-demo' if os.path.exists('/tmp/selected-graph')
                                else 'DEFAULT-hugegraph')
              ip = self.server.server_address[0]
              # broken-<ip>: every Gremlin call fails. flip-odd-<ip> /
              # flip-even-<ip>: the odd or even calls fail, counted from
              # the first call made while the file exists, so two Pods
              # on opposite phases are never healthy in the same sweep.
              odd = os.path.exists('/tmp/flip-odd-' + ip)
              even = os.path.exists('/tmp/flip-even-' + ip)
              n = calls[ip] = (calls.get(ip, 0) + 1) if (odd or even) else 0
              broken = (os.path.exists('/tmp/broken-' + ip)
                        or body.get('aliases', {}).get('graph') != expected_alias
                        or (odd and n % 2 == 1)
                        or (even and n % 2 == 0))
              if broken:
                  self._send(400, b'{"exception":"Could not rebind [graph]"}')
              else:
                  self._send(200, b'{"result":{"data":[0]}}')
          def log_message(self, *a):
              pass
      for ip in sys.argv[1:]:
          s = http.server.HTTPServer((ip, 8080), H)
          threading.Thread(target=s.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
      time.sleep(3600)
      PY
      python3 /tmp/fixture.py 127.0.0.1 127.0.0.2 127.0.0.3 &
      sleep 1
      run_hook() {
        PATH="/tmp/stub:${PATH}" PASSWORD=ci-password HG_TEST_DEADLINE_S=8 \
          STUB_IPS="$1" sh "${2:-/tmp/hook.sh}"
      }
      # Healthy: three Pods, all Gremlin-bound.
      run_hook "127.0.0.1 127.0.0.2 127.0.0.3"
      # One Pod answers REST but not Gremlin: the hook must fail.
      touch /tmp/broken-127.0.0.3
      if run_hook "127.0.0.1 127.0.0.2 127.0.0.3"; then
        echo "expected the hook to fail on a broken-binding Pod" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      rm /tmp/broken-127.0.0.3
      # Fewer Pods than the replica floor: the hook must fail.
      if run_hook "127.0.0.1"; then
        echo "expected the hook to fail below the replica floor" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      # Alternating health: sweep 1 sees A ok, B broken; sweep 2 sees A
      # broken, B ok; and so on. No single sweep is clean, so the hook
      # must fail. A hook that remembered earlier successes per Pod would
      # pass here after the second sweep.
      touch /tmp/flip-even-127.0.0.1 /tmp/flip-odd-127.0.0.2
      if run_hook "127.0.0.1 127.0.0.2 127.0.0.3"; then
        echo "expected the hook to fail when no sweep is completely healthy" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      rm /tmp/flip-even-127.0.0.1 /tmp/flip-odd-127.0.0.2
      # Dual-stack: each Pod publishes an IPv4 and an IPv6 address. Two
      # Pods give four addresses, which must not satisfy a floor of
      # three; three Pods must pass without the IPv6 addresses being
      # queried (nothing listens on them, so a query would fail).
      if run_hook "127.0.0.1 127.0.0.2 ::1 ::2"; then
        echo "expected the hook to count Pods, not addresses, on dual-stack" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      run_hook "127.0.0.1 127.0.0.2 127.0.0.3 ::1 ::2 ::3"
      # A non-default graph space must query the explicitly selected graph.
      # A missing alias still fails rather than weakening the per-Pod sweep.
      touch /tmp/selected-graph
      for alias in team_a-demo team_a-missing; do
        helm template ci helm/hugegraph -s templates/tests/test-connection.yaml \
          --set-string server.graphSpace=team_a \
          --set-string "server.testGraphAlias=${alias}" > "/tmp/hook-${alias}.yaml"
      done
      python3 - <<'PY'
      import yaml
      for alias in ('team_a-demo', 'team_a-missing'):
          d = yaml.safe_load(open('/tmp/hook-' + alias + '.yaml'))
          open('/tmp/hook-' + alias + '.sh', 'w').write(d['spec']['containers'][0]['command'][2])
      PY
      run_hook "127.0.0.1 127.0.0.2 127.0.0.3" /tmp/hook-team_a-demo.sh
      if run_hook "127.0.0.1 127.0.0.2 127.0.0.3" /tmp/hook-team_a-missing.sh; then
        echo "expected the hook to fail on a missing selected graph" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      rm /tmp/selected-graph
      # The auth-off render must carry no credentials.
      if helm template ci helm/hugegraph -s templates/tests/test-connection.yaml \
          --set hubble.enabled=false --set server.auth.enabled=false | grep -q 'Authorization'; then
        echo "the auth-off hook render must not carry credentials" >&2
        exit 1
      fi

  - name: legacy --reuse-values compatibility
    shell: 'bash -e {0}'
    run: |
      # A release created before a field existed must still render. This has
      # regressed five times, so it is guarded here rather than by review.
      # `-f` is NOT equivalent: it merges over the new defaults, whereas
      # --reuse-values discards them, so the fixture must become values.yaml.
      LEGACY_ROOT=$(mktemp -d)
      cp -R helm/hugegraph "$LEGACY_ROOT/chart"
      cp helm/hugegraph/testdata/values-pre-hardening.yaml "$LEGACY_ROOT/chart/values.yaml"
      helm template legacy "$LEGACY_ROOT/chart" > /dev/null
      LEGACY_UPGRADE=$(helm template legacy "$LEGACY_ROOT/chart" --is-upgrade)
      # The non-root PD and Store images need fsGroup on their data volumes
      # even when the reused values predate that default.
      [ "$(grep -c 'fsGroup: 10001' <<<"$LEGACY_UPGRADE")" -eq 2 ] || {
        echo "PD and Store must keep fsGroup 10001 under --reuse-values"
        exit 1
      }
